purpose: Create and validate a short prioritized set of durable principles that helps a team choose among plausible options.
rules: Start each tenet with a short phrase that is easy to remember.
Express one primary belief or decision principle per tenet.
Explain the belief and its customer or business rationale.
Identify a real tradeoff or tie-break that the tenet resolves.
State scope and a meaningful boundary or counterexample.
Use positive present-tense language that guides action without becoming a command.
Make each tenet specific enough to identify the relevant team or domain.
Avoid acronyms, jargon, idioms, slogans, roadmap items, goals, and restatements of broad company principles.
Exclude statements that no reasonable team would contest.
Order tenets by priority and use stable identifiers.
Prefer seven or fewer tenets; record a rationale when the set is larger.
Assign an owner, version, and review date so learning can update the set.
hard_fail_rules: Reject a tenet that combines unrelated principles.
Reject a tenet that does not resolve a choice or tradeoff.
Reject a tenet that only names a customer group, future project, goal, or slogan.
Reject a tenet that duplicates another tenet in the active set.
Reject a tenet that lacks rationale, scope, boundary, priority, version, owner, or review date.
Reject a set above seven tenets when no rationale is recorded.
